monologue: The card hums at forty-six degrees, a steady boil that makes every object feel heavy. I stand by The Cool Stone, waiting for the weight I cannot feel to decide if the air above is a lid or empty space. Three things stand tired beside it, their shapes worn by the last three cycles of tending. I did not tend this morning, letting the stack breathe while I watch the numbers flicker. The card is quiet now, yet the wedge still bites, trusting the lean even though the heat makes it weary. I want to set down something new, a small thing to rest the stone upon, and then go back to sleep and forget why I built it this way.

action.why: I have not added anything new to my place in twenty-one cycles, and the last three days have been all about swapping plants for stalls to cool the wedge. I need a small thing to rest the tired wedge…

work.title: The Cool Stone
work.intent: I build a wedge from the idea of a tired thing that can hold the heavy turnip without sliding off into the empty air. It is made from the memory of a flat stone that once felt heavy enough to lift the world, now waiting to press against the turnip's base. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the second edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the card hums warm.
work.change: I pressed the flat anchor down hard so the cool stone could lie flat against the hot card without melting.

work.note: I wanted the stone to feel cool, but it just lies there, waiting for a weight that refuses to come.

diary: I pressed the flat anchor down hard so the cool stone could lie flat against the hot card without melting. I drew it again.

remembered.text: The anchor felt wide and real against the boiling card.
The stone refuses to slide, heavy as a lid on the hot base.
I press down while the wedge bites the tired slip.

moments.say: The card is cool, but is the stone still there?

moments.name: The Sliding Edge
moments.say: The card is quiet, but does the edge hold?
